name: Neal Aronson
current_role: Founder and Managing Partner, Roark Capital Group (Atlanta)
profile: Neal Aronson (b. 1965) founded Atlanta private-equity firm Roark Capital in 2001 and remains its majority owner. Roark specialises in franchised brands and owns Subway, Arby's, Jimmy John's, Sonic, Dunkin' and Baskin-Robbins (via Inspire Brands), having done many of the restaurant industry's biggest deals of the past decade.
interesting_fact: Roark Capital is named after Howard Roark, the uncompromising architect-hero of Ayn Rand's The Fountainhead.
deep_cut_fact: Before Roark, he co-founded U.S. Franchise Systems in 1995 with his uncle Mike Leven (ex-Holiday Inn president), growing a 27-hotel regional chain (Microtel) into the 10th-largest US hotel franchisor with 1,100+ properties before selling to Hyatt's Pritzkers in 2000. He began his career in Drexel Burnham Lambert's corporate finance department.
notes: Low public profile; best route is Roark's media contact at Joele Frank. Franchise focus (restaurants, services) — not energy, but large real-asset/consumer deal-maker.
